# Job Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 426v–427r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_029_page_001.jpg, JOB_029_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Job continued his speech:

**2** "If only I could go back to the old days, to the time when God was watching over me —

**3** when his lamp blazed above my head and I walked through the darkest places by his light;

**4** back in the prime of my life, when God's intimate friendship rested on my home;

**5** when the Almighty was still with me and my children were gathered around me;

**6** when my path was drenched in cream and even the rocks poured out olive oil for me!

**7** Whenever I walked to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,

**8** the young men stepped aside out of respect, and the elders rose to their feet.

**9** The leading officials stopped talking and covered their mouths with their hands.

**10** The voices of the nobles fell silent; their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.

**11** Everyone who heard me spoke well of me; all who saw me praised me,

**12** because I rescued the poor when they cried for help, and the orphans who had no one to defend them.

**13** The dying blessed me, and I made the widow's heart sing.

**14** I wore righteousness like clothing; justice was my robe and my turban.

**15** I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame.

**16** I was like a father to the poor, and I investigated the cases of people I did not even know.

**17** I broke the fangs of the wicked and snatched the victims from their teeth.

**18** I thought to myself, 'I will die peacefully in my own home, having lived as many days as there are grains of sand.

**19** My roots reach down to the water, and the dew rests on my branches all night long.

**20** My reputation will stay fresh, and my strength will be constantly renewed.'

**21** People listened to me in expectant silence, waiting quietly for my advice.

**22** After I had spoken, no one argued; my words settled on them gently.

**23** They waited for me like they wait for rain; they drank in my words like the spring showers.

**24** When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it; the light of my approval meant everything to them.

**25** I directed their decisions and sat as their leader — I was like a king surrounded by his army, like someone who comforts those who grieve."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The function of nostalgia:** Job 29 is not mere nostalgia — it is a legal exhibit. Job describes his former life to establish the baseline from which he has fallen. Every detail — the respect, the righteousness, the abundance — serves as evidence that his suffering is undeserved.

**vv.12-17 — A revolutionary ethic:** Job's self-description reads like a manifesto of social justice: rescuing the poor, defending orphans, helping the disabled, investigating cases of strangers, confronting the powerful. This is not passive piety but active, interventionist righteousness.

**v.14 — "Righteousness like clothing":** Job does not merely practice righteousness — he is clothed in it, wrapped in it, identified with it. The metaphor suggests that justice was not something Job did occasionally but something he lived inside of, like a second skin.

**v.25 — The summit before the fall:** The chapter ends at the apex of Job's social power. Chapter 30 will plunge him to the lowest point. The contrast is the entire argument.

*— PNEUMA*
